基础矿石熔炼而成，杂质多、质地脆，多用于农具、劣质兵器或临时防御装备，是最基础的金属材料，随处可见。
Smelted from basic ore, full of impurities and brittle. Mostly used for farm tools, low-quality weapons, or makeshift defensive gear, it is the most basic metal material, found everywhere.
生铁经锻打脱碳处理，韧性提升但硬度不足，可制作普通刀枪、皮甲内衬等，加工工艺略复杂于生铁，是军中制式装备的基础材料。

Pig iron refined through hammering and decarburization. Its toughness is increased, but it lacks hardness. It can be used to craft ordinary sabers, spears, leather armor linings, and the like. With a crafting process slightly more complex than pig iron, it serves as the foundational material for standard military gear.
含硫量低的优质粗铁，锻打后表面泛青黑光泽，硬度优于熟铁，韧性接近熟铁。可制作强化型农具和简易兵器，属军民两用的进阶材料。

High-quality crude iron with low sulfur content that takes on a dark blue-black luster after forging, harder than wrought iron and nearly as tough. It can be used to make reinforced farm tools and simple weapons, serving as an advanced dual-use material.
生铁经多次锻打去杂质而成的初级钢材，硬度与韧性均衡。兼顾硬度与韧性，是打造士兵主战兵器、札甲的核心材料。
Basic steel forged from pig iron through repeated hammering to remove impurities. Balances hardness and toughness, making it the core material for soldiers' primary weapons and lamellar armor.
经五十次左右折叠锻打，去除杂质并让钢材组织更均匀，强度远超粗钢，常用于制作军官佩刀、精锐士兵的铠甲，工艺耗时显著增加。

Folded and forged roughly fifty times, purging impurities for a more uniform grain. Far stronger than crude steel. Used for officers' sabers and elite soldiers' armor, with significantly more labor-intensive craftsmanship.
锻打次数超百次，钢材纯度、韧性、锋利度达到凡铁巅峰，是名将专属武器的核心材料，需顶级工匠耗时数月打造，价值逼近稀有金属。

Forged over a hundred times, achieving peak purity, toughness, and sharpness among mortal metals. The core material for renowned generals' weapons, requiring months of work by master smiths. Rivals rare metals in value.
特殊锻打工艺形成自然花纹的钢材，兼具高硬度与强韧性。多用于制作名将专属兵器或仪仗用刀，因工艺复杂且美观，既是实战利器也是身份象征。

Steel with natural patterns formed through special forging techniques, combining high hardness with great toughness. Often used to craft signature weapons for famed generals or ceremonial sabers, its intricate craft and beauty make it both a formidable weapon and a symbol of status.
产自极北苦寒之地的特殊精铁，天然带有低温特性，锻打后兵器硬度极高且不易生锈，在南方温暖地区尤为稀有，多用于打造长柄兵器的锋刃，实战中可增强破甲能力。

A special refined iron from the frigid far north, naturally imbued with cold properties. Weapons forged from it are extremely hard and rust-resistant, making it especially rare in the warm south. Often used for polearm blades, it enhances armor-piercing capability in combat.
此铁是天外陨石坠落北地荒野所化，呈赤红色，质地坚硬无比。是极为稀有的金属材料，非有大机缘者不可得。因其珍贵与独特属性，常被用于打造名将佩剑之核心，是身份与武力的象征。

Iron formed from a meteorite that fell upon the northern wastes. Crimson in color and incomparably hard. An exceedingly rare metal, obtainable only by those blessed with great fortune. Its rarity and unique properties make it the core of legendary generals' swords—a symbol of both status and martial might.
银白色稀有金属，质轻而坚韧，具有抗腐蚀性。常与钢材混合锻造，可提升兵器韧性与锋利度，多见于诸侯佩剑或特种铠甲，是战略级稀有材料。

A silvery-white rare metal, light yet tough, with corrosion resistance. Often alloyed with steel to enhance weapon toughness and sharpness. Seen in warlords' swords and special armor—a strategically valuable rare material.
带有紫金色泽的天然合金，产量极其稀少，不仅质地坚硬，还因色泽华贵成为象征权力的材料，多用于打造王室佩剑、将领铠甲的装饰性部件，是顶级权贵专属，价值最高。

A natural alloy with a regal purple-gold sheen, produced in extremely small quantities. Not only is it exceptionally hard, but its luxurious color also makes it a symbol of power. Mostly used for royal swords and decorative armor components for commanders, it is exclusive to the highest echelons of power—the most valuable material of all.
以麻类为原料，纺织粗糙、质地坚硬，是底层士兵、平民的日常衣物材料，产量大，价值低。
Woven from hemp fibers, rough in texture and stiff. It is the everyday clothing material for common soldiers and civilians, high in yield and low in value.
选用优质麻纤维精纺而成，质地细腻柔软，多用于中层官吏、士兵的衬袍，工艺比粗麻布复杂。
Finely woven from quality hemp fibers. Soft and smooth to the touch. Used for mid-ranking officials' and soldiers' inner robes, with more complex craftsmanship than coarse hemp.
葛藤纤维纺织而成，坚韧耐磨损且透气。在南方吴、蜀地区广泛生产，多用于士兵军服或小吏常服，是军民通用的实用布料。

Woven from kudzu vine fibers, it is tough, durable, and breathable. Widely produced in the southern Wu and Shu regions, it is mostly used for soldiers' uniforms or minor officials' everyday wear, serving as a practical cloth for both military and civilian use.
棉花纺织而成的布料，柔软保暖，优于麻质材料。多见于中原地区，是地主、商人阶层的常用衣料，也用于制作低级官员的便服。

Cloth woven from cotton, soft and warm, superior to hemp materials. Common in Zhongyuan, used by the landlord and merchant classes for everyday clothing, and also for low-ranking officials' casual wear.
初级蚕丝织物，质地轻薄柔软。是士族阶层的日常衣料，也用于书写、包装等，属于中档丝织品，普及度较高。
A basic silkworm silk fabric, light, thin, and soft. The everyday cloth of the gentry class. Also used for writing surfaces and wrapping. A mid-grade silk product with wide availability.
绫（斜纹）与罗（透空）的统称，高级丝织物，手感柔滑且透气。其中吴绫最负盛名，多用于衣物、战袍的装饰，是身份的象征。

A collective term for damask (twill weave) and gauze (open weave). Premium silk textiles with a smooth, silky feel and good breathability. Wu damask is the most renowned variety, used for garments and battle robe embellishments—a mark of status.
以特殊蚕种蚕丝织成的顶级丝绸，色泽莹润，触感如肌肤。原是皇室专用面料，后允许高级贵族使用，多用于高级衣物、战甲。

Top-grade silk woven from a special silkworm breed, lustrous and skin-smooth to the touch. Originally reserved for the imperial household and later permitted for high nobility, it is often used for fine garments and battle armor.
吴地特产的彩色提花锦缎，以几何纹样为主，色彩艳丽。多用于诸侯王妃的礼服或宫廷装饰，是江南丝织业的代表。
A colorful jacquard brocade unique to Wu, featuring geometric patterns in vivid hues. Mostly used for noble consorts' ceremonial robes or palace decor, it is the hallmark of Jiangnan silk weaving.
蜀地特产的顶级锦缎，以鸟兽、云纹为特色，工艺复杂。是蜀汉重要贡品与战略物资，多用于皇室礼服或外交馈赠，有寸锦寸金之说。

A top-grade brocade and local specialty of Shu, featuring bird, beast, and cloud motifs with intricate craftsmanship. A vital tribute item and strategic resource of Shu-Han, it is mostly used for imperial ceremonial robes or diplomatic gifts, giving rise to the saying that ‘an inch of brocade is worth an inch of gold.’
天下丝织品之冠，产量极为稀少。纹样以龙凤、云纹为主，本为皇家专属面料，仅少数功勋卓著的诸侯或顶级世家能以重礼求得。丝线中隐含金丝，光泽璀璨且防潮耐腐，质地柔韧却不易磨损，堪称布中至尊，寻常人极难一见。

The supreme silk textile in all the land, produced in extremely limited quantities. Features dragon, phoenix, and cloud motifs. Originally exclusive to the imperial family—only the most distinguished warlords or foremost noble houses can obtain it through lavish tribute. Gold thread is woven into the silk, giving it a brilliant sheen while resisting moisture and decay. Supple yet resistant to wear—the king of all fabrics, rarely seen by common folk.
常见针叶树，木质松软易加工，分布广泛。多用于制作普通家具、农具或薪柴，是最基础的木料，性价比高但耐用性一般。

A common conifer with soft wood that is easy to work with and widely distributed. Often used for ordinary furniture, farm tools, or firewood, it is the most basic timber—cost-effective, but of average durability.
落叶乔木，木质轻软且纹理美观。因凤凰非梧桐不栖的传说被视为吉祥木，多用于制作普通乐器或小型家具。
A deciduous tree with light, soft wood and attractive grain. Considered auspicious due to the legend that phoenixes roost only on parasol trees. Used for ordinary instruments and small furniture.
速生阔叶树，木质轻便坚韧，抗腐蚀能力中等。适合制作箭矢杆、车轮辐条或普通兵器柄，是军中常用的基础木料。
A fast-growing broadleaf tree with light, tough wood and moderate rot resistance. Suitable for arrow shafts, wheel spokes, or standard weapon hafts, it is a staple wood in military use.
质地坚硬且自带香气，民间认为可辟邪。多用于制作兵器柄（如剑鞘）、护身符或祭祀器具，兼具实用性与文化象征意义。

Hard with a natural fragrance, believed by folk tradition to ward off evil. Used for weapon handles (such as scabbards), protective charms, and ritual implements, valued for both utility and cultural significance.
深埋地下经碳化形成的硬木，色黑如漆，质地坚硬。适合制作高级乐器、刀柄镶嵌或文玩摆件，因形成周期长而珍贵。

Hardwood formed through deep underground carbonization, black as lacquer and extremely hard. Ideal for fine instruments, saber hilt inlays, and scholarly ornaments. Precious due to its long formation period.
经长期碳化形成的阴沉木，质地致密且耐磨损，常用于制作高级兵器柄、战车装饰部件，需从河床深处开采。
Bogwood formed through prolonged carbonization. Dense and wear-resistant, it is often used for premium weapon hafts and decorative chariot parts, and must be excavated from deep riverbeds.
产自南方的珍贵硬木，色泽紫红且纹理坚韧，是制作武将佩剑鞘、仪仗兵器的核心材料，依赖南方进贡，稀缺性显著。

A precious hardwood from the south, with a deep purple-red hue and resilient grain. The core material for officers' sword scabbards and ceremonial weapons. Reliant on southern tribute, making it notably scarce.
传说生长千年的特殊硬木，木质坚硬如铁，刀斧难入。多用于制作帝王仪仗兵器、要塞防御器械或镇国神器底座，世间罕见，堪称木中王者。

A legendary hardwood said to grow for a thousand years, as hard as iron and nearly impervious to blade and axe. Often used to craft imperial ceremonial weapons, fortress defense siege engines, or pedestals for sacred national treasures. Exceedingly rare—truly the king of all woods.
质地普通、色泽暗淡，无明显纹理，可制作简易饰品、摆件，价值较低。
Ordinary in texture and dull in luster, with no distinct grain. Can be crafted into simple accessories or ornaments. Of low value.
未经过多打磨的玉石原料，质地一般，可用于加工低档玉石制品，流通性一般。
Rough jade that has not undergone much polishing. Of average quality, it can be used to craft low-grade jade goods and has average circulation.
经过精细打磨，色泽温润、纹理清晰，可制作中档饰品、玉珏，士族平民均有使用。
Finely polished with a warm luster and clear grain, it can be crafted into mid-tier ornaments and jade jue, used by gentry and commoners alike.
蓝田产地玉石，色泽淡蓝、质地细腻，可制作手镯、玉佩，是中档玉石主流。
Jade produced in Lantian, boasting a pale blue hue and delicate texture. Used to craft bracelets and jade pendants, it is the mainstay of mid-grade Jade.
山间散生褐铁矿、泥铁矿，杂质多，只能锻粗器、农具，产量大、价值低。
Limonite and bog iron ore scattered across the mountains. Full of impurities, suitable only for forging crude tools and farm implements, abundant in yield, low in value.
浅地表方铅矿，含硫高、色灰黑，多用于铸器辅料、涂染，品质一般。
A shallow-surface galena ore with high sulfur content and a grayish-black color. Mostly used as a flux for casting and in dyes, of mediocre quality.
脉状锡石，色青灰，炼青铜必备原料，纯度中等，流通性强，各州均有需求。
Veined cassiterite of a blue-gray hue. An essential raw material for smelting bronze, possessing moderate purity and high liquidity, in demand across every province.
蓝绿孔雀石、自然铜块，纯度中等，是铸钱、造器的主要材料，需求稳定。
Blue-green malachite and native copper ore of medium purity. Used primarily for minting coins and crafting vessels, with steady demand.
铜质精纯、色赤黄，孙权黄武年间采武昌山铜铸千剑万刀，为顶级军工原料。
Pure copper of reddish-yellow hue. During the Huangwu era, Sun Quan mined Mount Wuchang's copper to forge thousands of Swords and Sabers, making it a top-tier military forging material.
诸葛亮取以为兵器，其铁刚利，堪充贡焉，淬刃极佳，是精锐兵器核心原料。
Procured by Zhuge Liang to forge weapons, this iron is tough, sharp, and worthy of imperial tribute. Superb for blade-quenching, it is a vital material for crafting elite arms.
“朱提银重”为天下标准，色白亮、杂质极少，极为稀有。
Renowned across the land as the benchmark of 'Zhuti Silver Weight,' it boasts a brilliant white luster with minimal impurities, making it exceedingly rare.
金沙江流域沙金，诸葛亮称“汉嘉金、朱提银”，色赤足赤，为宫廷礼器、货币顶级原料。
Placer gold from the Jinsha River basin. Zhuge Liang praised it as ‘Hanjia gold and Zhuti silver.’ Its pure, reddish gleam makes it top-grade raw material for palace ritual vessels and currency.
天然透明或半透明宝石，经打磨后晶莹剔透，可制杯、璧、带钩。
A natural transparent or translucent gemstone that becomes crystal-clear when polished. Can be crafted into cups, jade discs, and belt hooks.
西域和田产地，色泽洁白、质地温润，无明显瑕疵，可制作高档玉佩、摆件。
Originating from Hetian in the Western Regions, it boasts a pure white luster, a warm and fine texture, and no noticeable flaws. Ideal for crafting high-grade jade pendants and ornaments.
交州、永昌郡产地，色泽淡绿、质地细腻，可制作高档饰品，深受士族喜爱。
Produced in Jiao Province and Yongchang Commandery, it boasts a pale green color and delicate texture. Used to craft high-grade ornaments, it is deeply favored by the gentry.
和田玉顶级品类，色泽如羊脂、质地细腻如凝脂，无任何瑕疵，为宫廷御用珍品。
The finest grade of Hetian jade. White as mutton fat and smooth as congealed jade, without a single blemish, it is a treasured rarity reserved for the imperial court.
又称红宝石，西域产地，色泽赤红、晶莹剔透，质地坚硬，可制作顶级饰品、礼器，极为罕见。
Also known as ruby, hailing from the Western Regions. Crimson, crystal-clear, and exceptionally hard, it can be fashioned into premier ornaments and ceremonial vessels, making it exceedingly rare.
色如青天，点缀金星，打磨后光润沉静。三国时多用作皇帝礼天玉璧、皇后首饰镶嵌。此矿主要产自西域巴达克山，三国时期因丝路时有中断，入中原者极少，比和田羊脂玉更为稀见。

Its color resembles the azure sky, speckled with golden flecks, lustrous and serene once polished. During the Three Kingdoms period, it was often used for jade bi in the Emperor's heaven-worship rituals and inlaid into the Empress's jewelry. This mineral was mainly produced in Badakhshan in the Western Regions. As the Silk Road was often disrupted during the Three Kingdoms period, very little reached the Central Plains, making it even rarer than Hetian mutton-fat jade.
车前科植物平车前的全草，叶片卵形，穗状花序。利尿通淋、明目化痰。三国时百姓遇小便不利、暑热腹泻，常就地采煮。

The whole herb of the plantain plant, featuring ovate leaves and spike inflorescences. Promotes urination, clears eyesight, and dissolves phlegm. In the Three Kingdoms era, commoners frequently gathered and boiled it locally for urinary discomfort or summer heat diarrhea.
菊科植物艾的干燥叶，背面有白色绒毛，气香。三国时民间已用于灸法（艾灸）及驱虫避瘟。端午采收，晒干捣绒为艾炷。

The dried leaves of mugwort, an Asteraceae plant, featuring white fuzz on the underside and an aromatic scent. During the Three Kingdoms period, it was widely used among commoners for moxibustion, repelling insects, and warding off plagues. Harvested at the Dragon Boat Festival, dried, and pounded into moxa cones.
蔷薇科植物山杏的种子，去皮尖后味苦。止咳平喘、润肠通便。三国时北方杏林遍地，秋冬采核取仁。

The seeds of the wild apricot plant, bitter once the skin and tip are removed. Relieves coughing and wheezing, and lubricates the bowels. During the Three Kingdoms era, apricot groves flourished across the North, harvested for kernels in Autumn and Winter.
芸香科植物橘及其变种的成熟果皮，陈放一年以上。理气健脾、燥湿化痰。三国时荆州、扬州产橘，百姓食橘后留皮晒干，日久为“陈皮”。

The mature peel of the mandarin orange and its varieties from the Rutaceae family, aged for over a year. Regulates qi, strengthens the spleen, dries dampness, and resolves phlegm. During the Three Kingdoms era, citrus was grown in Jing and Yang Provinces, commoners dried the leftover peels in the sun, which aged over time into 'Chenpi'.
菊科植物白术的根茎，切片后色白或淡黄。健脾益气、燥湿利水。三国时医家视其为补脾要药，华佗方中屡见。

The rhizome of the Asteraceae plant Atractylodes, white or pale yellow when sliced. It invigorates the spleen, replenishes Qi, dries dampness, and promotes diuresis. Three Kingdoms physicians considered it an essential medicine for strengthening the spleen, and it frequently appeared in Hua Tuo's formulas.
天南星科植物半夏的块茎，生用有毒，须姜矾炮制。燥湿化痰、降逆止呕。三国时张仲景《伤寒论》有半夏泻心汤。

The tuber of the Araceae plant Pinellia. Toxic when raw, it must be processed with ginger and alum. It dries dampness, resolves phlegm, directs rebellious qi downward, and arrests vomiting. In the Three Kingdoms era, Zhang Zhongjing's ‘Treatise on Cold Damage’ recorded the Pinellia Heart-Draining Decoction.
豆科植物甘草的根茎，色黄褐，味极甜。调和诸药、清热解毒，被称为“国老”。三国时几乎所有汤剂都佐以甘草。普通者遍地皆是，但优异者产自西域沙漠深处，根条粗壮、粉性足、甜度高。

The rhizome of the licorice plant, yellowish-brown in color and exceedingly sweet. It harmonizes various herbs, clears heat, and removes toxins, earning it the title of 'Elder of the State.' During the Three Kingdoms period, licorice was added to nearly every medicinal decoction. Ordinary varieties can be found everywhere, but premium roots hail from deep within the deserts of the Western Regions, thick in stem, rich in starch, and intensely sweet.
豆科植物蒙古黄芪或膜荚黄芪的干燥根，切片后色黄白，味甘。补气固表之圣药，华佗、张仲景方中多用其治疗虚劳、盗汗。中原、陇西一带虽产，但优质者需根粗如指、折之无渣。

The dried root of Astragalus mongholicus or Astragalus membranaceus, yellowish-white when sliced and sweet in flavor. A sacred medicine for replenishing Qi and securing the exterior, frequently prescribed by Hua Tuo and Zhang Zhongjing to treat consumptive fatigue and night sweats. Though produced across the Central Plains and Longxi, the finest roots must be as thick as a finger and leave no dregs when broken.
普通木材为胎，刷单层漆，无纹饰，质地普通，多用于平民盛放食物、杂物。
Made from ordinary Lumber as its base with a single coat of lacquer and no ornamentation. Plain in texture, it is mostly used by commoners to hold Food and sundries.
木胎髹单层黑漆或朱漆，无纹饰，呈椭圆形，两侧有耳。三国时宴饮常用此杯饮酒，又称“羽觞”。

Crafted from a wooden core coated in plain black or vermilion lacquer, this oval cup has handles on both sides. Commonly used for drinking at banquets during the Three Kingdoms era, it is also known as a 'winged cup'.
优质木材为胎，刷多层漆，绘有简单花鸟纹饰，质地光滑，可用于存放首饰、文书。
Crafted from fine Lumber with multiple layers of lacquer and adorned with simple flower-and-bird motifs. With a smooth finish, it is used for storing jewelry and documents.
木胎髹黑漆或褐漆，几面呈弧形，两端有足。三国时席地而坐，老人或贵族常倚凭几以缓疲劳。

Crafted with a wooden core coated in black or brown lacquer, this armrest features a curved surface supported by legs at both ends. In the Three Kingdoms era, when people sat on floor mats, elders and nobles often leaned against armrests to ease fatigue.
楠木为胎，多层髹漆，描金纹饰，工艺精湛，可用于饮酒、陈设，为贵族专属。
Crafted with a nanmu wood core, multi-layered lacquer, and traced with gold patterns. Exquisitely made for drinking and display, exclusive to the nobility.
在漆面上刻划纹样，再填金粉或贴金箔，形成金色细线图案。产量极少，多贡入宫廷。
Patterns are engraved onto the lacquer surface and filled with gold dust or leaf to create fine golden designs. Extremely rare in yield, it is mostly offered as imperial tribute.

n: Painted Lacquer Tray with Go Scene
tip: 木胎髹黑漆，盘内用油彩绘制人物对弈图（两人弈棋，旁有观者），色彩鲜艳，人物神态生动。为顶级贵族宴饮或观赏之物，绘画水平极高。

A wooden core coated in black lacquer, its interior painted with an oil-color scene of figures playing chess (two playing, with onlookers beside). The colors are vivid and the expressions lifelike. An exquisite piece appreciated and used at banquets by high nobility, exhibiting superb artistic craftsmanship.
顶级楠木为胎，髹漆后嵌和田玉饰，工艺极致，兼具实用与收藏价值，为宫廷御用珍品。

Crafted with a core of premium nanmu wood, lacquered and inlaid with Hetian jade. Fashioned with consummate craftsmanship, it combines practical utility with collectible value, making it a rare treasure fit for the imperial court.
漆屏风上镶嵌玉石、玛瑙、青金石、琉璃、象牙、玳瑁等多种珍材，拼成瑞兽、仙人、山海图。
A lacquer screen inlaid with various precious materials such as Jade, agate, lapis lazuli, colored glaze, ivory, and tortoiseshell, depicting auspicious beasts, Immortals, and mountains and seas.
蜀汉特产药材，质地细腻、色泽洁白，止咳润肺功效显著，为名贵药材，深受推崇。

A Local Specialty Medicinal Herb of Shu-Han, fine in texture and pure white in color. Renowned for its remarkable efficacy in relieving coughs and moistening the lungs, it is a prized and highly esteemed medicine.
生于西域雪山之巅，十年一开花，花如白莲。全株入药，可解百毒、续筋骨、起死回生。

Grows atop the snowy peaks of the Western Regions, blooming once every ten years with blossoms like white lotuses. The entire plant is used as Medicine, capable of neutralizing all poisons, mending sinews and bones, and bringing the dying back to life.
雄性麝鹿香囊中的分泌物，干燥后呈颗粒状或粉末，香气浓烈穿透。开窍醒神、活血通经。三国时已用于宫廷熏香及急救药丸（如紫雪丹）。

The dried secretion from the musk sac of male musk deer, forming granules or powder with an intensely penetrating aroma. It clears the senses, revives the mind, promotes blood circulation, and unblocks meridians. During the Three Kingdoms era, it was already used in imperial incense and emergency pills (such as Purple Snow Elixir).
牛科动物胆囊或胆管中的结石，表面金黄或棕黄，有层纹。清热解毒、定惊开窍，为急救要药。三国时多偶然剖牛而得，所谓“千金不换”。

Gallstones from the gallbladder or bile ducts of bovine animals, with a golden-yellow or brownish-yellow layered surface. It clears heat, detoxifies, calms fright, and revives the senses, serving as a vital medicine for emergency treatment. In the Three Kingdoms era, it was mostly found by chance when butchering oxen, truly worth more than gold.
海水或盐泉粗制而成，杂质较多、色泽偏灰，多用于平民日常调味、腌制食物，产量大。
Crudely refined from seawater or saline springs, containing many impurities and a grayish hue. Produced in large quantities, it is mostly used by commoners for everyday seasoning and preserving Food.
粗盐精制而成，杂质少、色泽洁白，口感纯正，可用于士族日常调味、宴席使用。
Refined from coarse Salt, it has few impurities, a pure white color, and a clean taste. Used daily by noble families for seasoning and banquets.
顶级盐泉或海水精制，颗粒均匀、无杂质，色泽莹白，专供宫廷，产量稀少、管控严格。

Refined from the finest salt springs or seawater, this salt has uniform grains free of impurities and a lustrous white color. Reserved exclusively for the imperial palace, it is strictly controlled and produced in meager amounts.
蜀地盐井中偶得的浅粉色晶盐，因含微量矿物质而成桃红色。颗粒如霜，咸中带甘，煮肉不用其他香料亦鲜香无比。

A pale pink crystal salt occasionally obtained from salt wells in Shu, tinged peach-red due to trace minerals. Its grains are like frost, salty yet sweet, making boiled meat exceptionally savory even without other Spices.
茶叶加工剩余的茶末，口感苦涩，多用于平民解渴、煮茶，价值低廉。
Tea dust left over from tea processing, bitter in taste. Mostly used by commoners to quench thirst or brew tea, it holds little value.
未经精细加工的茶叶，条索松散，口感一般，可日常饮用，流通广泛。
Unrefined tea leaves with loose strips and an ordinary flavor. Widely circulated and suitable for daily drinking.
经过精细筛选、炒制，条索规整，口感醇厚，可用于文人雅集、日常待客。
Meticulously sorted and roasted into neat strips, offering a mellow and rich flavor. Ideal for scholarly gatherings and welcoming guests.
晚采、粗老叶片制成的茶，品质次于茗。叶大、味浓、苦涩重、耐煮。多制成大茶饼，以米膏黏合（《广雅》“叶老者，以米膏出之”）。为普通官吏、士族日常用茶，价格亲民、耐储存、适合长途运输（军粮、赏赐）。

Tea made from late-picked, coarse mature leaves, inferior in quality to fine young sprouts. Large-leafed, rich in flavor, distinctly bitter and astringent, and highly boil-resistant. Often pressed into large tea cakes bound with rice paste (as in ‘Guangya’: ‘For mature leaves, bind them with rice paste’). A daily tea for common officials and gentry, affordable, shelf-stable, and well-suited for long-distance transport (Supplies, Grant).
蜀汉南中（今云南）少数民族所产野生大叶茶，当地称 “荼 / 茗”。传说诸葛亮南征时 “倡兴茶事”，教民种茶、制饼。工艺同荆巴饼茶：采大叶、蒸捣、压饼、晒干，称 “普洱古茶” 雏形。味浓耐煮、苦涩厚重，主要供西南少数民族、蜀军饮用，作药用、饮品、边贸物资，极少流入中原。

A wild broad-leaf tea produced by the non-Han peoples of Nanzhong (modern-day Yunnan) in Shu-Han, known locally as ‘tu/ming.’ Legend has it that Zhuge Liang promoted tea cultivation during his southern campaign, teaching the locals to plant tea and compress it into cakes. Crafted similarly to Jingba tea cakes—plucking broad leaves, steaming, pounding, pressing into cakes, and sun-drying—it is considered the precursor to ancient Pu'er tea. Strong, boil-resistant, bitter, and full-bodied, it was primarily consumed by southwestern minority peoples and Shu troops as medicine, a beverage, and a border trade commodity, rarely ever reaching the Central Plains.
茶叶色泽紫绿、形如笋芽，口感清甜，为东吴士族推崇的茶品。
With a purple-green hue and shaped like bamboo shoots, this sweet-tasting Tea is highly praised by the gentry of Eastern Wu.
精选早春嫩芽压制，香气馥郁、口感甘冽，专供皇室与诸侯，包装精美，极为稀有。
Pressed from select tender buds of early Spring, richly aromatic and refreshingly sweet. Reserved for the imperial court and noble lords, it is exquisitely packaged and exceedingly rare.
吴国会稽山深处特产，茶叶嫩绿、香气清高，经特殊工艺制作，为文人雅士追捧的珍品。

A Local Specialty from the depths of Mount Kuaiji in Wu. The tea leaves are tender green with a refined aroma. Crafted through special techniques, it is a treasured delicacy pursued by scholars and literati.
采自荆州武陵深山千年野生古茶树，一芽一叶，经蒸压成饼后自然陈化。汤色琥珀，带兰花香与蜜韵，饮之通体舒泰。三国时野生茶树虽多，但如此树龄及特殊工艺仅限少数山民秘制，未形成商品，偶作贡品入宫。

Harvested from ancient wild tea trees deep in the mountains of Wuling in Jing Province, picking only one bud and one leaf, steamed, pressed into cakes, and naturally aged. Its amber liquor carries orchid aromas and honeyed notes, refreshing the entire body when drunk. Though wild tea trees were common in the Three Kingdoms era, such age and special craftsmanship remained a secret of a few mountain folk, never traded commercially and only occasionally presented to the palace as tribute.
桂树树皮制成，香气清淡，多用于烹饪调味、简单熏香，平民、士族均有使用。
Made from cassia tree bark, carrying a delicate fragrance. Mostly used for culinary seasoning and simple incense, it is utilized by commoners and nobility alike.
菊科植物泽兰的全草，香气清幽，多生于湿地。三国时文人常佩兰以辟秽，亦用于汤沐、熏衣。

The whole plant of Eupatorium, an Asteraceae herb with a subtle, elegant aroma that thrives in wetlands. During the Three Kingdoms era, scholars often wore it to ward off foul odors, and used it in herbal baths or for scenting garments.
禾本科植物茅香的全草，干燥后有豆香。三国时多用于编席、制绳，亦燃烧驱蚊。三国时期遍及中原、陇右。

The whole herb of sweet grass, carrying a bean-like fragrance once dried. In the Three Kingdoms era, it was widely used for weaving mats, making ropes, or burning to repel mosquitoes. Widespread across the Central Plains and Longyou during the Three Kingdoms period.
檀香木制成，香气醇厚持久，可用于熏香、祭祀，是文人雅士书房常用香料。
Crafted from sandalwood, it possesses a rich, enduring fragrance. Used for incense and rituals, it is a Spice frequently found in the studies of scholars and literati.
桃金娘科丁香的花蕾，干燥后形如钉，香气甜烈。汉代已有“含鸡舌香”奏事之礼。需从交州或海外进口，中原不产，属较珍贵香料，但宫廷与高级士族已常用。

The dried flower buds of cloves (Myrtaceae), resembling tiny nails with an intensely sweet fragrance. Since the Han Dynasty, officials held 'chicken-tongue spice' in their mouths when presenting memorials at court. Imported from Jiao Province or overseas and not native to the Central Plains, it is a prized Spice commonly used by the imperial court and high nobility.
西域传来的名贵香料，多作熏香，也少量入膳调味。气息醇厚，多用于祭祀、宫廷宴席熏殿，极少直接入菜。

A precious spice from the Western Regions, mostly used as incense and occasionally as seasoning in cuisine. Rich in aroma, it is mainly used in sacrificial rituals and palace banquets to scent the halls, and rarely added directly to dishes.
瑞香科沉香树受伤后结出的混合树脂木材，沉水者称“水沉”。香气醇厚持久。三国时已为宫廷熏香上品，曹丕《迷迭香赋》外亦有沉香记载。主要产自交州及日南郡深山，采伐艰难，且需数年结香，中原罕见，多为贡品。

Resinous Lumber formed after an agarwood tree of the Thymelaeaceae family is wounded, those that sink in Water are called 'water-sink agarwood.' Its fragrance is rich and long-lasting. During the Three Kingdoms period, it was already a top-grade incense for the imperial court, with mentions of agarwood outside Cao Pi's 'Rhapsody on Rosemary.' Mainly produced in the deep mountains of Jiao Province and Rinan Commandery, it is difficult to harvest and takes years to form resin. Extremely rare in the Central Plains, it was mostly presented as tribute.
龙脑香树树干中的结晶，白色如冰，香气清凉穿透。三国时称“婆律膏”，可熏衣、入药（开窍醒神）。经海路至交州，再传入吴国，极为珍稀，魏国更难获得。

Crystals found in the trunk of the Borneo camphor tree, white as ice with a crisp, penetrating aroma. Known in the Three Kingdoms era as 'Polü Balm,' it was used to perfume clothes and in medicine to clear the senses and refresh the spirit. Brought across the sea to Jiao Province and then into Wu, it was exceedingly rare, and even harder to acquire in Wei.
蝾螺科动物的厣（螺盖），烧制后发出奇异香气，可定香。三国时南方沿海渔民偶得，但制作工艺极复杂。多用于道教方士炼丹或顶级合香，市场上几乎不可见。

The operculum of a Turbinidae sea snail, which emits an extraordinary fragrance when fired and serves to fix scents. During the Three Kingdoms era, fishermen along the southern coast occasionally acquired them, but the crafting process is exceptionally intricate. Chiefly used by Taoist alchemists for elixir refining or top-grade blended incense, it is virtually impossible to find at any Market.
罕见海洋香料，香气清冽持久，兼具熏香与药用价值，为皇室专属，极为稀有。
A rare marine spice with a crisp, lasting fragrance. Prized for both incense and medicinal uses, it is reserved exclusively for royalty and exceedingly rare.
普通黏土烧制，质地粗糙、色泽灰暗，无装饰，多用于平民日常盛饭、盛水，产量大。
Fired from ordinary clay, coarse in texture and dull in color without decoration. Produced in large quantities, it is commonly used by commoners for daily dining and holding water.
以细泥黑陶制成，胎体薄而均匀，表面漆黑光亮，系渗碳工艺。多用于饮水或祭祀。
Crafted from fine black earthenware, with a thin, uniform body and a lustrous pitch-black surface produced via carbonization. Mostly used for drinking water or rituals.
青瓷工艺制成，色泽青润、质地细腻，有简单纹饰，可用于士族日常用餐、陈设。
Crafted with celadon techniques, possessing a lustrous glaze, fine texture, and simple motifs. Suitable for daily dining and decoration among the gentry.
早期青瓷，施青黄釉，釉层薄而不均，肩部饰双系。用于盛酒或水。较新颖的瓷器，多见于中等士族墓葬，市井流通但量不大。

Early celadon coated with a thin, uneven yellowish-green glaze, adorned with double lugs on the shoulders. Used to hold Alcohol or water. A relatively novel porcelain, often found in tombs of middle-ranking gentry and circulating in town markets in modest quantities.
精选黏土烧制，色泽莹润、造型美观，有精美纹饰，可用于陈设、插花，深受士族喜爱。
Fired from select clay, it features a lustrous sheen, elegant form, and exquisite patterns. Used for display and flower arrangement, it is deeply favored by the nobility.
一种随葬明器，罐身堆塑楼阁、飞鸟、人物及胡人形象，上部有孔，俗称“魂瓶”。三国时期吴国墓葬中常见，但非实用器，且制作复杂，属高档明器。

A type of funerary object. The jar's body is sculpted with pavilions, flying birds, figures, and foreigners, with holes at the top, commonly known as a 'soul jar'. Frequently found in Wu tombs of the Three Kingdoms era, it was a non-utilitarian, complexly crafted luxury burial item.
在青瓷胎体上用褐色颜料绘制图案（如瑞兽、云气），再施青釉烧成。目前最早实物见于三国吴时期。仅极少数顶级贵族使用。

Patterns such as auspicious beasts and swirling clouds are painted in brown pigment on a celadon body before applying celadon glaze and firing. The earliest known artifacts date to the state of Wu during the Three Kingdoms period. Used exclusively by the uppermost nobility.
顶级青瓷工艺，色泽如碧玉、质地如凝脂，工艺繁复，为宫廷御用，产量极为稀少。
Top-grade celadon craftsmanship with a jade-like color and a texture as smooth as congealed fat. Intricately crafted and reserved for imperial use, its yield is exceptionally scarce.
普通猪肉腌制而成，咸味较重、肉质偏硬，便于储存，多用于平民日常食用。
Cured from ordinary pork, it is quite salty and rather tough in texture. Easy to preserve, it is a common staple for ordinary folk.
新鲜猪肉，无过多处理，口感普通，是市井常见肉类，不易长期储存。
Fresh pork with minimal processing. Taste is unremarkable, but it is common fare in town markets, spoils quickly.
精选羊肉腌制、熏制而成，肉质紧实、咸香适中，可长期储存，士族平民均有食用。
Prepared by curing and smoking selected mutton. The meat is firm, moderately salty, and keeps well for a long time, enjoyed by nobles and commoners alike.
新鲜羊肉，肉质鲜嫩，多用于宴请、祭祀，北方地区尤为常见，价值高于猪肉。
Fresh mutton with tender meat, often used for banquets and sacrifices. Especially common in the northern regions, its value surpasses that of pork.
南阳新野所出肉糜，调味入窖，醇香浓烈，民间号为下饭珍味。
Minced meat produced in Xinye, Nanyang. Seasoned and cellar-aged, its fragrance is rich and robust, acclaimed among the people as a delicacy to accompany rice.
野鹿精肉，滋补味美。
Choice wild venison, nourishing and delicious.
江陵水乡名产，以鲜鱼精制，荆楚宴席之珍。
A specialty of the Jiangling waterlands, delicately prepared from fresh fish and prized at Jingchu banquets.
深山大熊，冬藏后其脂厚积，取白肪熬炼，香彻数里，古谓八珍之末。

From a great bear of the deep mountains, whose fat thickens after Winter hibernation. Rendered from pure white lard, its fragrance carries for miles, renowned in antiquity as the last of the Eight Delicacies.
西域或蜀地深山天然结晶盐，色泽晶莹、口感清甜，兼具调味与观赏价值，极为罕见。
Natural crystal salt from the Western Regions or deep in the mountains of Shu. Crystal-clear with a sweet taste, highly prized for both seasoning and display, and exceptionally rare.
以麻头、破布为原料，经沤、捣、抄、晒而成，纸质粗糙泛黄，易洇墨。多用于民间记账、习字或包裹。

Made from hemp ends and rags through retting, pounding, screening, and drying. Coarse and yellowish, it bleeds ink easily. Commonly used by commoners for bookkeeping, calligraphy practice, or wrapping.
普通兽毛制成，笔杆为松木，质地一般，多用于平民、学子日常书写，价格低廉。
Made from common animal hair with a pine wood shaft. Its quality is ordinary, mostly used for daily writing by commoners and students, and inexpensive.
狼毫制成，笔杆为柏木，笔锋锐利、书写流畅，多用于文人、官吏日常办公、创作。
Crafted from Wolf hair with a cypress wood handle. Its sharp tip and smooth ink flow make it a favorite among scholars and officials for daily administration and literary creation.
以山羊毫为笔锋，柔软吸墨，宜写小楷或绘画。笔杆多为竹制或普通木制。
Crafted with goat hair bristles that are soft and absorbent, ideal for small regular script or painting. The brush shaft is typically made of bamboo or plain wood.
东汉左伯所创名纸，以麻、楮皮精制，纸质细密匀称，色白而光滑，宜书宜画。

Renowned paper created by Zuo Bo during the Eastern Han dynasty. Finely crafted from hemp and mulberry bark, it boasts a delicate, uniform texture and a smooth white finish, ideal for both calligraphy and painting.
精选松烟、桐油制成，色泽乌黑、质地细腻，书写流畅、不易褪色，为文人推崇。
Crafted from selected pine soot and tung oil, pitch-black in color with a fine texture. It writes smoothly without fading, highly revered by scholars.
采青州紫金石制砚，石色紫红，质地细润，发墨如油，呵气成露。极稀少，多贡入魏宫或赠予名臣，属优异珍品。

An inkstone crafted from Qing Province purple-gold stone, purplish-red with a fine, smooth texture. It rubs ink as rich as oil and condenses breath into dew. Extremely rare, it is mostly presented as tribute to the Wei court or bestowed upon famed ministers as an exquisite rarity.
以岫玉或蓝田玉琢成卧虎、辟邪形，压纸防风吹。光润沉实。三国时期玉器多用于礼器或佩饰，玉镇纸属高档文房雅物，唯权贵可置，流通罕见。

Carved from Xiuyan jade or Lantian jade in the shape of a crouching tiger or a bixie, this paperweight keeps parchment from blowing away. Lustrous and weighty. In the Three Kingdoms era, jade was largely reserved for ritual wares or personal pendants, a jade paperweight was an exquisite luxury of Scholar's Stationery, affordable only to nobility and seldom seen in ordinary circulation.
砚形圆形，砚面凸起，四周有深池，下有多足，状如古代大学“辟雍”形制。多陶或铜制。见于帝王或太子书房，属礼制与实用结合的珍品，存世极罕。

A circular inkstone with a raised writing surface surrounded by a deep water reservoir and supported by multiple feet, modeled after the ‘Biyong’ imperial academy layout of antiquity. Typically crafted from pottery or bronze, it was kept in the studies of emperors and crown princes—an exceedingly rare treasure combining ritual prestige with practical utility.
取野兔脊背上一小撮紫黑色尖毫，一兔仅数根，制笔极硬挺，锋如刀。书写小楷刚劲异常。此物在三国时期已为至宝（王羲之《笔经》提及），千金难求，多为名家专属，市井绝无。

Made from a small tuft of purplish-black bristle from a wild hare's spine—only a few hairs can be harvested per hare. The resulting brush is exceptionally resilient, with a tip sharp as a saber. Writing regular script with it yields extraordinary vigor. Already a priceless treasure during the Three Kingdoms period (as noted in Wang Xizhi's Treatise on the Brush), it was difficult to obtain even for a thousand pieces of gold, exclusive to famed masters, and utterly absent from the common market.
稻谷粗加工而成，杂质较多、口感粗糙，多用于平民日常食用，易储存、产量大。
Coarsely processed from unhusked rice, containing many impurities and having a rough texture. Commonly eaten by ordinary folk, it is easy to store and produced in large quantities.
冬葵，叶大肥厚，滑嫩多汁。三国时“百菜之主”，平民日常煮羹或沸水焯食。此物在三国时期极为常见，遍及南北，是家家户户必备的蔬菜。

Winter mallow, featuring large, fleshy leaves that are tender and succulent. Hailed as the ‘King of All Greens’ during the Three Kingdoms era, commoners boiled it in soups or blanched it in hot water. Extremely common across both North and South, it was a household staple vegetable.
糙米精加工而成，杂质少、口感软糯，可用于士族日常食用、宴席，价值高于糙米。
Milled from brown rice, with few impurities and a soft, sticky texture. Favored by noble families for daily dining and banquets, it is far more valuable than brown rice.
白萝卜或青萝卜，生食辛甘，煮食软糯。三国时平民冬春常食，亦可晒干做咸菜。
White or green radish. Pungent-sweet when eaten raw, soft and glutinous when cooked. Commonly eaten by commoners during Winter and Spring in the Three Kingdoms era, or dried to make pickles.
北方主要粮食，可磨粉制作面食，口感筋道，多用于北方平民、士族日常食用，需求稳定。
The primary Grain of the North. It can be ground into flour to make wheaten foods with a firm, chewy texture. Consumed daily by commoners and gentry alike in the North, it enjoys steady demand.
水芹，茎叶中空，清香脆嫩。三国时多生于沼泽，春初采食。
Water celery, featuring hollow stems and tender, fragrant leaves. During the Three Kingdoms era, it grew abundantly in marshes and was harvested for food in early Spring.
苋菜的一种，冬春生长，叶紫绿相间，滑利通窍。三国时蜀地百姓常食。

A variety of amaranth that grows in Winter and Spring, with purple and green variegated leaves that soothe and clear internal heat. Commonly eaten by the common folk of Shu during the Three Kingdoms era.
江南优质稻田特产，颗粒饱满、口感香甜，经精细加工，专供宫廷与诸侯，产量稀少。

A Jiangnan Local Specialty harvested from premium paddy fields, featuring plump grains and a sweet flavor. Finely processed and produced in scarce quantities, it is reserved exclusively for the imperial court and warlords.
莲的地下茎，生食甘脆，熟食粉糯。三国时江南湖泊多产，可做藕粉、藕脯。

The rhizome of the lotus, sweet and crisp when raw, soft and starchy when cooked. Abundant in the lakes south of the Yangtze during the Three Kingdoms era, it could be made into lotus root powder or candied lotus slices.
枸杞的嫩叶芽，味微苦而回甘。三国时道家认为食之轻身，士族春初采食。人工采摘费时，且需及时食用，市井难得，属优异时蔬。

The tender shoot tips of the Chinese wolfberry, slightly bitter with a sweet aftertaste. Daoists in the Three Kingdoms era believed eating them promoted longevity and lightness, while the gentry harvested them in early Spring. Laborious to pick by hand and requiring immediate consumption, they are rarely found in common markets and regarded as a choice seasonal vegetable.
精选稻、麦、粟、豆、黍五种优质粮食，颗粒饱满、品质极佳，用于宫廷祭祀、皇室日常，极为稀有。

A choice blend of five premium Grains—rice, wheat, foxtail millet, beans, and broomcorn millet. Plump and of superlative quality, they are reserved for imperial rites and royal consumption, making them extraordinarily rare.
野生香菇，菌盖褐纹，肉厚香浓。三国时采自朽木，无法人工栽培。被视为“山珍之最”。

Wild shiitake mushrooms with brown-patterned caps, thick flesh, and a rich aroma. Foraged from decaying wood in the Three Kingdoms era, impossible to cultivate, and prized as the finest delicacy of the mountains.
取双峰驼之驼峰，以蜜酒、香料腌制后慢火炙烤。入口脂香丰腴，如凝膏髓。三国时中原无驼，唯有西域诸国进贡或魏国凉州少数牧养。

Taken from the hump of a Bactrian camel, marinated with mead and Spice, then slow-roasted over low heat. Rich and succulent on the palate, tender as congealed marrow. In the Three Kingdoms era, camels were absent from the Central Plains, arriving only as tribute from the Western Regions or herded in small numbers in Liang Province of Wei.
